answers.answer: 1) Start with 25 money, 1 active worker on the notepad and 3 inactive workers below it. 2) Draw 8 Zoo cards, keep 4 and discard 4; draw 2 hidden Final Scoring cards. 3) Put Animals I in slot 1, the other four Action cards randomly in slots 2–5, all side I. 4) Appeal starts staggered by turn order at 0, 1, 2, 3.

1) Face-up base projects: 4 in a four-player game, 3 in two- or three-player games. 2) In two players only, block one level on each of the three face-up projects (left, middle, right respectively) and the three donation spaces in the left column; none are blocked at setup in three or four players. 3) Reveal the six-card display after everyone chooses their starting hand.

1) Using slot 4: take its card out, move cards from slots 1–3 one slot right, then put the used card in slot 1. 2) Set action strength before acting; each X-token adds 1 strength, may be spent in any quantity, and max holding is 5. X-tokens gained during the action cannot boost it. 3) Resolve after-finishing effects only after the action and card movement are complete.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure; X-tokens; After finishing effects

answers.answer: 1) You cannot choose a regular action that plays zero animals or builds zero buildings; taking zero is not legal. 2) Instead take exactly 1 X-token, selecting an Action card and moving it to slot 1 with intervening cards shifted right. Slot strength/upgraded side do not matter. 3) Cannot take this action if already holding 5 X-tokens.

1) Upon reaching the last Break space, ignore excess steps and gain 1 X-token. 2) Finish the current turn, then conduct the break. 3) After the break, reset token to the player-count start space and continue clockwise with the next player.
answers.evidence: Break track; Break trigger from effects

answers.answer: 1) Both Cards sides advance Break token 2 spaces; break movement grants no money on Cards I. 2) I: draw per strength table (max 3) with possible discard, OR at strength 5+ snap exactly one display card of any reputation. II: draw from deck and/or within reputation range; snap exactly one any-reputation display card from strength 3, with no deck draw. 3) II draw is reputation-limited but snap is not. 4) Display replenishes at turn end. Hand limit applies only at breaks (3, or 5 with hand-limit university).
answers.evidence: CARDS action; Special Rules: Display timing and Hand size

answers.answer: 1) In-range display means the folder matching your reputation and all lower-numbered folders. 2) Reputation 10+ requires upgraded Cards action. 3) Beyond space 15, remain there and gain 1 appeal per further reputation. 4) You may not inspect the discard pile during play.

1) Build I builds exactly one building up to strength; Build II builds different building types totaling at most strength, no duplicate type in that action. Cost is 2 money per space. 2) First building must touch a border space; later ones must edge-touch an existing building. 3) Cannot cover map water/rock, occupied spaces, go off-map; restricted-icon spaces require Build II. 4) Kiosks must be at least 3 spaces apart. Each pavilion gives +1 appeal immediately, once.

1) I offers standard enclosures, kiosk, pavilion, and one Petting Zoo per zoo. II additionally allows one Reptile House and one Large Bird Aviary per zoo. Supply has four tiles of each special type. 2) Build cannot create unique buildings; they enter via Sponsor cards. 3) Covering every map space except water/rock gives 7 appeal immediately.
answers.evidence: Buildings available through Build; Side II; Full zoo map

answers.answer: 1) Earlier action benefits may fund later steps (including money, cards, or activated workers), but each item must be paid before its own benefit is received. 2) Ordinary effects resolve immediately; after-finishing waits until the whole action and card movement complete. 3) For simultaneous effects, the owning player chooses their order.
answers.evidence: X-tokens paragraph; Animals action; Multiple simultaneous effects

answers.answer: 1) Check all left-side conditions, pay cost first, then house the animal legally. Matching partner zoo discounts 3 money per matching-continent icon, including doubled icons. 2) Standard enclosure must be empty and meet minimum size; admit animal then flip entire enclosure occupied. Petting Zoo animals only use Petting Zoo. 3) Reptiles/some birds may alternatively use indicated special housing if free capacity; mark each used space with a supply player token and never flip special enclosure. 4) Meet water/rock adjacency on selected housing, counting distinct adjacent terrain hexes. 5) Effects resolve after admission; immediate effects before the next animal, after-finishing effects after entire Animals action.

1) Animals II permits playing from display within reputation range, paying extra equal to folder number; hand/display mix is allowed and refill waits until turn end. 2) At strength 5+, may gain 1 reputation at the very start, before selecting animals, so range increases. 3) May play upgrade-condition animals.

1) Only immediately when constructing a Reptile House or Large Bird Aviary, relocate all eligible animals that fit, deciding each separately. 2) Meet terrain requirements and special-house capacity; mark occupied capacity with player tokens from supply. 3) For each animal, flip smallest occupied standard enclosure meeting all its requirements; if none, smallest meeting size; if none meets size, flip none.
answers.evidence: Moving existing animals into a newly built special enclosure

answers.answer: 1) Task strengths: reputation 2, partner zoo 3, university 4, project work 5. Side I exactly one task; side II one or more different tasks with total value no greater than strength, plus up to one donation. 2) Need active worker; if one of yours already on that task, use 2 workers; if 3 already there, unavailable until break. Opponents’ workers do not matter.

1) Take available tiles from Association board and place on lowest empty matching map spaces; resolve covered-space bonus immediately. University also gives its printed reputation immediately. 2) No duplicate universities; partner zoos must be different continents, max four; third/fourth require Association II. 3) Universities give research icons; only the hand-limit university raises limit from 3 to 5.

1) Support an in-play project or play a Conservation Project from hand and support it immediately (Association II may use in-range display for folder cost). New projects enter leftmost above board; push right, and if over capacity discard rightmost. 2) Meet a condition and take an unoccupied reward level; each project normally supported once, and each level holds one token total across players. 3) Put one of your left-map support tokens on condition; gain project reward and uncover its map bonus, in either order. Immediate bonus now; recurring-income bonus now and each break. 4) Overflow tokens return to owners’ supplies; map bonuses remain activated.
answers.evidence: Conservation project work; Overflow; Support procedure

answers.answer: 1) Release size category is based on printed standard enclosure requirement: 2− accepts 1 or 2, 3 accepts 3, 4+ accepts 4 or 5; not exact tile size. 2) Lose only printed appeal before conservation; discard animal and lose its icons, retaining conservation, reputation, ability-earned appeal and prior effects. New release project gives 1 reputation; later support does not. 3) If animal can use special housing and required tokens can be removed, must remove them; otherwise flip smallest occupied standard meeting all requirements, then size-only fallback, else none.

1) Sponsors I plays exactly one hand card if strength ≥ level and conditions met, or chooses break movement and takes money equal to strength. II plays one or more with strength +1 ≥ sum of levels; may use hand/display in range and pay folder cost per displayed card. 2) Resolve each sponsor fully before next, deferring after-finishing effects. 3) Break-money option on II pays twice strength even if only one space remains before end.

1) Break order: discard to hand limit; clear tokens on Action cards; recall workers/restock tiles; discard display folders 1–2, compact/refill; income; reset Break token. 2) Kiosk income is 1 per adjacent unique building, special enclosure, occupied standard enclosure, and pavilion; empty standard gives none, empty special counts. 3) For players receiving display cards during income, order clockwise from initiator (or first affected), refill after each such player before next affected player chooses.

1) Conservation 2: upgrade action or activate worker. At 5 and 8: choose 5 money or available bonus tile. At 10: everyone discards one Final Scoring card when first reached; if nobody reaches it, discard before final scoring. 2) Check end at own turn end or during break when appeal/conservation counters share or pass scoring area. Owner gaining appeal on another turn checks at own turn end or break. 3) Turn-trigger: triggering player completes turn and others take one; break trigger: all take one. 4) Each Final Scoring card capped at 4 conservation. VP = appeal minus lowest appeal in conservation counter’s scoring area; highest positive wins; tie by most projects supported, then shared.

1) Shuffle 9 tiles; place random face-up tiles on the four blank yellow spaces beside 5 and 8 conservation (two each); do not use two icon spaces; return five unused to box. 2) If a component supply runs out, use suitable substitute; physical stock alone does not prohibit legal play.

1) Advanced maps: take two random and choose one, or lay out player count +1 and select in reverse turn order. 2) Map A begins with empty 3-space enclosure and kiosk on indicated spaces; printed kiosk counts as built and place tile reminder.
1) Seven support tokens begin on designated spaces at left edge of map. 2) Hire inactive workers lowest supply space upward. 3) Some maps give conservation points when hiring last worker.
answers.evidence: Personal setup C2-C3; Association worker supply

answers.answer: 1) Flip chosen card I→II in its current slot. 2) Improved action is usable from next action, but counts as upgraded immediately for conditions; current action retains its starting strength/kind. 3) There are only four upgrade opportunities, so not all five can be upgraded.
1) Strength 1: draw 1/discard 1; 2: 1/0; 3: 2/1; 4: 2/0; 5+: 3/1. 2) Required discard may be a newly drawn card or one already in hand.

1) Categories include bird, herbivore, predator, primate, reptile, bear, and Petting Zoo animal. Bear remains a category even when combined with herbivore/predator; include both special categories unless excluded.

1) Association II permits exactly one donation only if at least one task was performed in same action; donation needs no worker. 2) Pay smallest visible amount: 2,5,5,7,7,10,10, then repeatable 12. Skip setup-blocked spaces; cover chosen space with supply token and gain 1 conservation. After other spaces covered, repeat donations cost 12 with no further tokens placed.

1) Count upper-right Animal/Sponsor icons; for Animals and unique-building Sponsors also upper-left water/rock requirements; plus partner zoo continent and university research icons. 2) Do not count left-side conditions or conservation-project icons; university reputation/hand-limit benefits are not icons. 3) Card’s own icons count; double icons count twice. Card text takes priority over general rules.
answers.evidence: Counting icons; Card text takes priority

answers.answer: 1) Count distinct adjacent water/rock hexes; multiple edges on one hex count once, and a larger region counts only actually adjacent hexes. 2) Decorative terrain illustrations on tiles do not count as terrain spaces/requirements.

1) Playing a new Release into Wild project gives its player 1 reputation; supporting an existing one does not. 2) Breeding Program family uses same condition on all three levels; choose any available reward space once condition met.
answers.evidence: Release into the wild; ALL Breeding Program project cards

answers.answer: 1) X:Y means left side is condition, right side reward. 2) No number or “per” condition pays once per fulfillment; numeric thresholds pay only once, and with multiple thresholds use highest met.

1) Connected = uncovered and edge-adjacent to covered space; isolated = no adjacent covered space. 2) Border space has at least one of six sides without neighboring map hex. 3) Your zoo includes your played cards, map, personal supply; any zoo means these for all players.

1) Unique buildings must be placed when Sponsor played, using matching tile colored face up, freely rotated but not flipped. 2) Ordinary placement/terrain rules apply, no size-based payment; unique buildings are not enclosures and cannot house animals or count as terrain. 3) If placement impossible, cannot play Sponsor.

1) Both granted actions happen after Animals action finishes and its card moves to slot 1. 2) Use granted action’s card normally and move it after that action. Named Action requires specified action and cannot be replaced by X-token action; Determination (Any Action) can choose any action including X-token.
answers.evidence: Base animal ability clarifications: Action / Determination

answers.answer: 1) Assertion searches unused face-down base-project deck and adds chosen project to hand; Dominance obtains named project from same deck, but has no effect if already in play. 2) Later play/support via Association, placing it above board, not in setup base row below.

1) Resolve after Animals and moving Animals card. Clever chooses a card and moves it to slot 1; cards formerly left shift right. Boost moves named card to slot 1 or 5; moving to 5 shifts cards formerly right left.

1) All four interactive abilities require affected zoo at least 5 appeal; multiplayer can replace interactive text with solo alternative on those cards. 2) Eligibility uses appeal before/after animal according to chosen order; new animal appeal may be resolved before or after ability.

1) Each affected other zoo meeting threshold places tokens on its own cards: ahead on one track, one on slot 5; ahead on both, one each on slots 4 and 5. 2) Never stack; duplicates return. Each token reduces action strength by 2 including each multiplied execution; X-tokens can restore. 3) Removed after acting or cleared at break.
1) At effective strength ≤0, use enough X-tokens to reach at least 1, choose X-token alternative, or leave card until it reaches slot 3 or higher.
answers.evidence: Constriction — affected players and card ownership

answers.answer: 1) Digging 2 allows up to two selections, choosing after each whether to discard/refill display or discard a hand card and draw deck card; may change option. 2) Display discard is replaced immediately, shifting folders down and drawing folder 6.

1) Flock animal can avoid new enclosure if another zoo herbivore requires at least its standard size; same host may host any number. 2) Without host, house normally; a later non-flock animal cannot join its enclosure. 3) On release no historical proof needed; release procedure frees occupied enclosure even if flock shared it.
1) Activate lowest remaining reserve worker onto notepad for immediate use. 2) Take map conservation reward for hiring last worker if printed. 3) If all workers active, no effect.
1) If none of the revealed cards is Animal, discard all revealed cards.

1) Choose target among tied highest-appeal qualifying zoos; if self, no effect. 2) Copy only target card in slot 1, 2, or 3; use target card’s side, but your own X-tokens. 3) Move targeted card to slot 1 normally. Venom/Constriction on it apply then are discarded; Multiplier cannot be used.

1) Place gained Multiplier on named card; bonus tile lets you choose any card including Animals. Next use executes twice successively at same base strength, move card only after both; each X-token boosts one execution. 2) Defer after-finishing effects until both done; break waits until whole turn finishes. 3) Return used tokens to supply; unused removed at next break.

1) Two Multiplier tokens add two executions: up to three total, not four. 2) X-tokens may be spent on multiplied regular executions; may multiply X-token alternative but cannot mix one X-token action with a regular action.

1) Peacocking may place Large Bird Aviary before Build II, only if no Aviary already and legal site. 2) Other placement restrictions remain, including Build II for restricted spaces. Posturing follows normal rules including kiosk spacing; place multiple buildings sequentially.
1) First, second, third Petting Zoo animal grant 3, 6, 9 appeal respectively. 2) One Petting Zoo holds max three; these animals count as small.

1) Acting player chooses among tied leaders separately for each target selection. Pilfering 1 targets highest appeal; 2 separately highest appeal and most conservation, each target at least 5 appeal. 2) Zero-conservation leader is ineligible; if all zero, that part has no effect. 3) Self-target has no effect.

1) Target chooses five money or random hand-card draw; never Final Scoring. 2) If no hand cards, give money; with less than five money, give card; with neither, give all money including zero. 3) Resolve repeat pilferings sequentially; target may choose differently each time.
1) Pouch cards tucked under animal lose all function; if animal released discard tucked cards too, but retain appeal earned. 2) Sunbathing sold cards go to discard pile.
1) Extra Final Scoring card drawn before 10-conservation milestone joins choices when discarding one. 2) At game end score every remaining Final Scoring card, each capped at 4 conservation.
1) Shuffle discard pile face down, draw randomly, select as card specifies, return discard pile face up; Scavenging 3 draws 3, keeps one and discards rest.

1) Snapping takes exactly one display card regardless reputation, not a deck draw. 2) Sponsor Magnet finds display Sponsors regardless reputation; if none, no effect. Ordinary end-turn refill applies.

1) Venom tokens go on lowest-slot cards in order, one per card; duplicate tokens return. 2) Using marked card removes token and avoids all Venom fees that turn, including X-token alternative (if under 5 tokens). 3) Pay 2 at turn end only if removed none and at least one remains. Unused tokens clear at next break.
1) Immediate: 2/5/10 money for 1/2/3 universities. 2) Project-support task strength becomes 4 instead of 5. 3) Final: 1 conservation for three universities.
1) Immediate reward: 2 appeal per previously supported project, counted by missing left-map tokens. 2) Break income: 1 conservation.

1) Count different continent and animal-category icon types together, each once; exclude research; doubled/repeated copies do not add types. 2) Gain 1 conservation per two types, rounding down; each other player gains 2 money per conservation you gain.
1) On play, gain 1 appeal per research icon. 2) Owner gains 2 money whenever any player plays a research icon. 3) Final: 1 conservation with five different animal categories.
1) Immediate: 1 appeal per Americas icon. 2) Each Americas icon played permits free kiosk under normal placement and spacing. 3) Final: 1 conservation with five or more kiosks.
1) Immediate: 1 appeal per Australia icon. 2) Each Australia icon played permits tucking one hand card under Sponsor for 2 appeal; tucked cards have no further function.

1) Each card stores two supply player tokens on itself when played. 2) When supporting a base project below Association board, return exactly one token as any one icon; cannot spend both for one project. Above-board cards originating from base deck do not qualify. 3) Final: 1 conservation with five or more project supports.

1) Each Build action may add one extra copy of a building built in that action without extra strength; pay normal cost and obey placement. 2) Only one extra building, and special-enclosure one-per-type limit still applies. 3) Final: 5 appeal with full map excluding water/rock.

1) Immediate: 2 money per water/rock icon. 2) May cover terrain spaces and ignore animal/unique-building terrain requirements; printed terrain icons still count. 3) Covered terrain no longer counts for Hydrologist, Geologist, Architectural Zoo. 4) Final: 2 appeal per water/rock icon pair, max 3 pairs.

1) Each actual placement bonus on border grants extra choice of any uncovered placement bonus on map, not necessarily border. 2) Multiple triggers give multiple choices; copied bonuses may be same or different. Resolve chosen order. 3) Final: 1 conservation when all building border spaces covered, excluding terrain.

1) Immediate: 1 X-token. 2) Each Release support grants 1 extra conservation; may support same release project repeatedly with different qualifying animals, max one token on project per Association action. Each token counts as separate support for other effects.

1) Immediate: 1 X-token. 2) Immune to Venom, Constriction, Hypnosis, Pilfering; for Hypnosis/Pilfering skip its counters and find next qualifying player. 3) Final: 1 conservation with all five continents.

1) Choose small or large permanently and mark box with supply token; reveal deck until that type found, keep it, discard others. 2) Cannot play opposite type. 3) Chosen small gain +2 appeal; chosen large +4; size 3 remains legal, no bonus.

1) Immediate: 2 money per small animal. 2) Animals action containing only small animals permits one extra small animal from hand, normal cost/rules. 3) Then may take small animal from display regardless reputation even if declined extra play.

1) Immediate: 1 appeal per water icon. 2) Each newly covered space adjacent to water gives 1 money, even multiple spaces in one building; adjacent to multiple water hexes still pays once. 3) Final: 1 conservation if all water hexes connected (none isolated).
1) Place unique Barred Owl Hut under normal rules. 2) Each bird icon played draws two deck cards, keeps one, discards the other.
1) Place unique Sea Turtle Tank adjacent to water. 2) Each reptile icon played permits selling up to two hand cards for 4 money each; discard sold cards.
1) Each predator icon played triggers Hunter with draws equal to total predator icons. A double predator icon triggers two sequential Hunters, counting both new icons each time.

1) Place building and three supply tokens on its card. 2) Per herbivore icon played, may spend token and pay money equal to hand Sponsor level to play Sponsor meeting conditions. 3) Its own icon can trigger on play; three total uses. Card source is hand.
1) Gain 1 reputation and 1 conservation; place Zoo School covering at least two border spaces. 2) Take one in-range display card or draw one deck card; simultaneous benefits may be ordered by you.

1) Unique building may be placed over two border spaces without touching existing building; other rules apply. 2) Later buildings may attach. 3) Break income is 2 money per adjacent building except empty standard enclosures; it may stand beside kiosk. Side Entrance itself counts as a building for adjacent kiosks. 4) Final: 5 appeal with full map except water/rock.

1) Immediate: 1 appeal per connected uncovered building border space, never water/rock. 2) Final: 1 conservation per six contiguous empty building spaces, evaluate each group separately. 3) Upgrade-restricted spaces count; terrain excluded.

1) Immediate: 2 money per different continent/animal-category icon; research excluded. 2) Each newly introduced category/continent gives 1 appeal and 2 money; double of same new icon gets novelty reward once.

1) Immediate: may place free size-5 standard enclosure under normal placement. 2) When playing large animal, ignore one left-side condition, not terrain. 3) Stacks with Research Institute to ignore two conditions.
1) Gain 1 conservation for each animal category with more icons than player to your right. 2) If they have none, one of yours suffices. 3) Maximum 4 conservation.

1) Observation Tower bonus applies only to standard enclosures adjacent to tower hex, not another rock hex. 2) Special enclosures do not qualify. 3) Refilling an emptied standard enclosure earns two appeal again. 4) Tower is not a building for kiosk income.

1) Standard enclosure touching Outdoor Area hex counts two spaces larger for all purposes after placement; adjacency to other water alone does not qualify. 2) Cannot ignore size on release/transfer. 3) No special enclosure effect; Outdoor Area is not building.

1) Building on Harbor-adjacent building space activates it; first building may start beside Harbor but need not. 2) Discard ability usable once per own turn, before/during/after action, not breaks/other turns. 3) Harbor is not building.

1) Restaurant break income is 1 money per adjacent covered hex, regardless type/occupancy; empty enclosures qualify and each hex counts separately. 2) Restaurant is not building and gives adjacent kiosks no income. 3) Special bonus grants one free Reptile House OR Large Bird Aviary, even before Build II; not both, normal other placement rules apply.

1) Cover H spaces with buildings under ordinary placement rules; reveal deck until Sponsor, keep it, discard others. 2) H is not placement bonus, so no Archaeologist trigger. 3) After all three H spaces covered, every Sponsor level is one lower. 4) Third/fourth partner still require Association II and restricted building spaces still require Build II.
1) Pay money equal to Sponsor level and meet usual conditions. 2) This bonus plays only from hand, even Sponsors II. 3) Sponsors action card stays in its slot; it does not move.
answers.evidence: Official base FAQ: bonus granting Sponsor

answers.answer: 1) Appeal cannot exceed 113 and conservation cannot exceed 41; gains beyond those track ends are lost.
answers.evidence: Official base FAQ: Appeal cannot exceed

answers.answer: 1) Venom affects every other zoo with higher appeal and at least 5 appeal. 2) Hypnosis targets highest appeal at ≥5, ties chosen by actor; self has no effect; copy only slots 1–3. 3) Pilfering 1 targets highest appeal; Pilfering 2 independently targets highest appeal and most conservation; each target ≥5, ties actor chooses, self no effect; conservation target must have ≥1. 4) Constriction affects each other zoo at ≥5 appeal ahead on appeal and/or conservation: one token on its slot 5 if ahead on one track, two on slots 4 and 5 if ahead on both.

1) Animal partner condition requires partner zoo from its continent; Sponsor partner condition accepts any continent. 2) Red maximum-25 condition allows play only while appeal ≤25; minimum reputation requires stated value. 3) −1 ignores one left-edge requirement; all others including terrain remain.
answers.evidence: Official base FAQ: bonus icons and conditions

answers.answer: 1) Each of up to two selections chooses either discard one display card and immediately replenish it, or discard one hand card then draw one deck card. 2) Choose anew after each card.
1) Remaining display cards slide down to fill gaps while preserving their order; then empty folders are filled from deck.
answers.evidence: Reputation track and display; Display timing

answers.answer: 1) Build standard enclosure empty side up (yellow border/size number). 2) Each covered placement-bonus space grants its bonus immediately once; turning enclosure occupied later does not award again.
1) Discard one Final Scoring card face down under the remaining Final Scoring card pile.

1) Randomly determine start player; thereafter clockwise, one turn at a time. 2) No formal rounds. 3) Each turn takes one action using one of five Action cards; resolve additional effects/bonuses as the selected action and its effects direct.
1) If nobody reaches 10 conservation before game ends, all players must discard one Final Scoring card before end-game scoring begins.
